text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A central and local governments meeting on the planned highway between Tallinn and the second largest town Tartu decided that a $100 million loan would be needed for the reconstruction of the road to meet contemporary standards.
- Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi described integration into Europe as Estonia's first priority but admitted that relations with Russia needed improvement.
- The inhabitants of Tallin would prefer controversial Centre Party leader Edgar Savisaar to become their mayor, a poll commissioned by the Centre Party said.
- The Baltic Battalion will be continued after the current agreements expire in 1997, Defence Minister Andrus Aavel told a news conference.
- Vaehi sharply criticised the Reform Party and its ministers in the ruling coalition in an article accusing the Reformists of inefficiency.
- Estonia divided its embassy in Brussels to separate the embassy in Belgium and the mission to the EU.
- A presumed underworld boss was shot dead on Saturday by a hired killer, who escaped after firing seven shots.
- The Pala accident revealed inadequacies in telephone communications as the crash took place in an area out of wire or cellular telephone coverage. Similar areas exist in every county.

- Tallin court reversed a decision to seize 4,400 tonnes of fuel by the customs department from a fuel export firm as unconstitutional. The customs department pointed out that this precedent makes its work nearly impossible.
- A major Tallin cable TV firm stopped broadcasting Estonian TV programmes as the economic crimes police and local copyright protection firm considered such broadcasting illegal.
